task.description:
WF-03 STEP 4b -- TEST COVERAGE HARD GATE for ISS-0440. TEST-DESIGNER (step-04) reported PASS: 18 new tests in test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (43 passing in that file), full suite 3156 passed / 0 failures, lint 0 new violations, and three mutants measured in a throwaway git worktree -- M1 (@autofix_map widened to include FAIL => COMPLETED) 40/43, M2 (guard_empty_scope/2 neutered to always :ok) 40/43, M3 (print_autofix_report/1 neutered) 41/43.

YOUR CORE OBLIGATION, stated in WF-03 in capital letters and non-negotiable: 'TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must independently APPLY at least one of the reported mutants and run it -- accepting the reported pass counts is copying a claim, not validating one.' Do that. APPLY AT LEAST ONE MUTANT YOURSELF (M1 is the highest-value choice -- the FAIL refusal is the single safety property SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS rests on; apply a second if time permits) and REPRODUCE THE COUNTS. If your reproduced count differs from the reported one, that is a finding, not a rounding error -- report the exact numbers you measured and treat the discrepancy as at least MAJOR.

MUTANT HYGIENE IS PART OF THIS GATE, not an afterthought. WF-03: 'A mutant is a TEMPORARY PROBE. Leaving one in the tree is a step failure.' PREFERRED -- use a throwaway `git worktree` of this branch so the working checkout is never mutated; remove it when done. If you mutate in place instead, revert with `git checkout -- <path>` and VERIFY: quote `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty AND a green re-run of the test file against restored code, both in your result.summary. Also VERIFY TEST-DESIGNER's own cleanup: confirm the mutation worktree they used is actually gone (`git worktree list`) and that lib/ and test/ on this branch contain no mutant residue -- diff lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex against the step-03 committed state.

COVERAGE VALIDATION. The step-04 handoff's task.description lists 9 required coverage points. Walk them one by one against the ACTUAL test code -- read the tests, do not read TEST-DESIGNER's summary and agree with it. For each point state: which named test covers it, and whether that test actually DISCRIMINATES (would it fail if the behaviour were wrong?) or merely executes the path. Give particular scrutiny to:
  - Point 5 (FAIL refusal): the handoff required BYTE-IDENTITY asserted by reading the file before and after, not merely 'status is still FAIL'. Confirm the test does the strong assertion. Note that ISS-0442 (filed this run) establishes that --autofix REFORMATS a whole file when it does write, so a weak assertion here would be especially misleading.
  - Point 7 (nested result.status untouched): a file with top-level COMPLETED and result.status PASS must come back byte-identical. This is the exact confusion ISS-0440 is about; confirm it is genuinely tested.
  - Point 3 (empty scope raises): confirm the test asserts a raise, not just a non-zero-ish outcome.

THINGS THAT WOULD BE A FAIL: a coverage point with no discriminating test; a mutant count you cannot reproduce; mutant residue anywhere in lib/ or test/; any test that touches the real handoffs/ corpus or could run --autofix against it (grep the test file for @handoffs_dir / "handoffs" literals and check every hit); tests that pass for the wrong reason (e.g. a tmp-dir path that silently matches nothing -- TEST-DESIGNER reported hitting exactly this Windows Path.wildcard separator bug and fixing it with Path.expand/1, so verify the fix is real and applied everywhere, not just where it was noticed); missing on_exit cleanup leaving tmp dirs behind.

ALSO CHECK, briefly: that the new tests do not assert as DESIRED the behaviours ISS-0442 (whole-file reformat on autofix) and ISS-0443 (unknown flags silently ignored) exist to change. A test that pins the current reformat behaviour as an expectation would make ISS-0442 harder to fix later; if you find one, report it at MINOR with the test name.

RUN THINGS YOURSELF. Re-run `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` and quote the real output. Re-run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` and quote it. Do not inherit any number from step-04's summary without re-deriving it (docs/anti-patterns.md, 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source').

You may READ anything. Do not EDIT lib/ or test/ except as a temporary, reverted-and-verified mutant. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL in result.status and per-coverage-point verdicts in result.summary; on PASS route to TEST-RUNNER (step 04c). Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.

result.summary:
TEST COVERAGE HARD GATE VERDICT: PASS. Independently re-derived every claim in step-04's report against the actual test code and by running commands myself -- did not inherit any reported number without reproducing it.

RE-RUN mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (real output, quoted): "Result: 43 passed" (0 failures). Matches step-04's claim exactly.

RE-RUN mix letflow.lint_handoffs (real output, quoted): "letflow.lint_handoffs: OK -- 0 new violations across 1930 handoff files under \"handoffs\" (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190)." 0 new violations, consistent with baseline (file count grew from 1929 to 1930 purely from this run's own handoff commits since step-04, not a defect).

INDEPENDENT MUTANT REPRODUCTION (the core obligation of this gate). Used a THROWAWAY git worktree (../letflow-2-tdv-mutants, detached HEAD at this branch's own commit 363bf96f, deps/ and _build/ copied in so the working checkout was never touched) -- never mutated lib/ or test/ in the main working tree at any point.

Baseline in worktree before any mutant: mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs -> "Result: 43 passed".

M1 (applied myself, highest-value per the dispatch -- widened @autofix_map to add \"FAIL\" => \"COMPLETED\"): re-ran mix test myself. MY OWN MEASURED RESULT: "Result: 40/43 passed", with exactly these 3 named tests failing: T-AUTOFIX-EVERY-FIX-AND-REFUSAL-ON-STDOUT, F-RUN-AUTOFIX-SHAPE, T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-FAIL. This is an EXACT match to step-04's reported M1 count and failing-test set (40/43, same three names). Inspected the actual failure detail for T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-FAIL: "Expected exception Mix.Error but nothing was raised" -- confirms the mutant genuinely breaks the FAIL-refusal safety property (the file would have been silently rewritten and the run would have exited 0) and the test genuinely catches it. This is the central safety property SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS rests on, and it is demonstrably covered.

M2 (applied myself, second mutant, time permitted -- neutered guard_empty_scope/2 to unconditionally :ok): MY OWN MEASURED RESULT: "Result: 40/43 passed", with exactly these 3 named tests failing: T-DIR-EMPTY-SCOPE-RAISES, F-NONEXISTENT-DIR-RAISES, F-EMPTY-DIR-RAISES. Exact match to step-04's reported M2 count and failing-test set. Confirms the 'confident green for a scan that never happened' trap is genuinely caught.

Did not apply M3 myself (print_autofix_report/1 neutered) -- two independently-reproduced, exactly-matching mutants (covering the two highest-priority traps named in the dispatch: FAIL-refusal safety and empty-scope false-green) is sufficient corroboration per the dispatch's 'apply at least one, a second if time permits' instruction; M3's own stdout-visibility property is also incidentally exercised by M1's own failure of T-AUTOFIX-EVERY-FIX-AND-REFUSAL-ON-STDOUT (that assertion covers both a fix's and a refusal's stdout report, and failed under M1 specifically because the refusal never fired), giving indirect corroboration of the same stdout-report code path without needing a third independent worktree run.

MUTANT HYGIENE (verified myself, not inherited). After each mutant: git checkout -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex in the worktree, then re-ran mix test. QUOTED: after M1's revert, git status --porcelain lib/ test/ in the worktree returned EMPTY (no output); mix test re-run: "Result: 43 passed". After M2's revert, git status --porcelain lib/ test/ again EMPTY; mix test re-run: "Result: 43 passed". SHA256 comparison: main checkout's lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex and the worktree's restored copy both hash to 1c9cf92ab29221f7dcecad437fd85ff3302862570c0cf0b2f593f74032b46c22 -- byte-identical, matching the SHA256 step-04 itself quoted. Worktree then removed: git worktree remove --force ../letflow-2-tdv-mutants, confirmed absent from git worktree list afterward (only the three pre-existing unrelated agent worktrees remain). Main working tree: git status --porcelain lib/ test/ empty throughout this entire gate -- I never mutated it.

TEST-DESIGNER'S OWN CLEANUP VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: git worktree list shows no residual ../letflow-2-iss0440-mutants entry (TEST-DESIGNER's own worktree name) anywhere. git diff 4634eef9(step-03c REVIEWER PASS commit)..HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex is EMPTY -- the shipped lib file is byte-identical to the state REVIEWER passed; no mutant residue anywhere in lib/. git diff 4634eef9..HEAD --stat shows only test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (+343 lines), two new docs/issues/*.yaml files, and this run's own handoffs/ -- no new files under test/fixtures/lint_handoffs (confirmed via git diff --stat -- test/fixtures/, empty), consistent with TEST-DESIGNER's claim that no new fixture files were needed.

COVERAGE POINT WALK (read the actual test code, not step-04's summary; verdict on each: named test(s) + does it discriminate, i.e. would it fail if the behaviour were wrong):
  1. --dir <fixture> scans ONLY the fixture, banner names it -- T-DIR-SCOPED-SCAN: asserts io =~ inspect(dir), io =~ \"across 1 handoff files\", refute io =~ \"handoffs/WF\". DISCRIMINATES (would fail if scope leaked to the real corpus or the banner omitted the dir).
  2. --dir with no value Mix.raise-s -- F-DIR-MISSING-VALUE (resolve_dir/1 unit) + T-DIR-MISSING-VALUE-RAISES (run/1 end-to-end), both assert_raise Mix.Error with a message regex. DISCRIMINATES.
  3. --dir at a zero-file directory Mix.raise-s (not a clean OK) -- F-EMPTY-DIR-RAISES, F-NONEXISTENT-DIR-RAISES, T-DIR-EMPTY-SCOPE-RAISES, all assert_raise. DISCRIMINATES -- independently CONFIRMED by my own M2 run: neutering guard_empty_scope/2 drives exactly these three red, nothing else.
  4. --autofix rewrites PASS/COMPLETE/DONE -> COMPLETED -- T-AUTOFIX-PASS/COMPLETE/DONE, each decodes the rewritten file and asserts status == \"COMPLETED\". DISCRIMINATES.
  5. --autofix REFUSES FAIL, file BYTE-IDENTICAL -- T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-FAIL: reads raw file bytes before and after (File.read!/1, not Jason.decode!/1) and asserts after_content == before verbatim -- this is the strong byte-identity assertion the dispatch specifically required, not merely 'status is still FAIL'. Also asserts assert_raise Mix.Error and the refusal text on stdout. DISCRIMINATES -- independently CONFIRMED by my own M1 run, which broke exactly this property (the mutant made the write happen and the raise not fire; test failure: 'Expected exception Mix.Error but nothing was raised'). Given ISS-0442's finding that a real fix DOES reformat the whole file, this byte-identity check on the REFUSED path is exactly the right place for that strength of assertion (nothing is ever written to a refused file, so byte-identity is trivially achievable and correctly required) -- and critically, no FIXED-path test makes an equivalent whole-file-byte assertion (see the ISS-0442/ISS-0443 pinning check below), so this suite does not accidentally encode the reformat behaviour as a requirement anywhere.
  6. Legal-but-wrong / outside-map values untouched and refused -- T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-OUTSIDE-MAP, T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-LEGAL-BUT-WRONG-ENUM, both assert byte-identity via File.read!/1 == before. DISCRIMINATES.
  7. Nested result.status untouched -- T-AUTOFIX-DOES-NOT-TOUCH-NESTED-RESULT-STATUS: top-level COMPLETED with nested result.status: PASS, asserts the whole file is byte-identical before/after --autofix. This is the exact confusion ISS-0440 is about (nested result.status vs top-level status) and it is genuinely tested with a strong byte-identity assertion, not a weaker 'still says PASS somewhere' check. DISCRIMINATES.
  8. Every fix and refusal on stdout -- T-AUTOFIX-EVERY-FIX-AND-REFUSAL-ON-STDOUT plus per-case io =~ assertions in T-AUTOFIX-PASS/REFUSES-FAIL/etc. DISCRIMINATES -- independently CONFIRMED broken under my own M1 run (the stdout-report assertion in this same test also failed because the refusal branch never fired).
  9. Default no-flag path unaffected -- T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS, explicitly scoped cheap per the handoff's own instruction, relies on the pre-existing 'existing .json handoff behavior (H1-H5) is unaffected' and H6 describe blocks plus T-H6-ZERO-NEW already in this file (read and confirmed those blocks exist and still pass in this same run). Reasonable scoping, not a gap.

All 9 required coverage points map to a named, discriminating test. No coverage gap found.

HAZARD CHECKS (all clear):
  - Real-corpus touching: grepped the test file for the literal \"handoffs\" string -- exactly 3 hits, all safe: LintHandoffs.resolve_dir([]) == \"handoffs\" (pure string return, no I/O), LintHandoffs.guard_empty_scope(\"handoffs\", []) == :ok (pure function call, no scan), and an io =~ ~s(under \"handoffs\") assertion on T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS's stdout capture from a --autofix-less run([]) call, which that same test explicitly also asserts refute io =~ \"AUTOFIX\" on. No test in this file ever passes --autofix together with the real handoffs/ directory. CONFIRMED CLEAR.
  - Skipped tests / TODOs: grepped for @tag :skip and \"TODO\" in the new ISS-0440 section -- none found.
  - Shared hardcoded state / test ordering dependence: every ISS-0440 describe block's setup creates a fresh System.tmp_dir!/0 subdirectory with a unique integer suffix (System.unique_integer([:positive])) and Path.expand/1-normalizes it, torn down via on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(dir) end). No test reads state left by another test; async: true (module-level) confirms self-sufficiency was assumed by design and nothing here contradicts it.
  - Windows path-separator bug fix real and applied everywhere: grepped every new setup block in the ISS-0440 section -- all 4 (guard_empty_scope describe, run/1 end-to-end describe, run_autofix/1 describe, ISS-0440 tests generally) pipe System.tmp_dir!() |> Path.join(...) through |> Path.expand() before use. Confirmed no setup block omits it.
  - ISS-0442/ISS-0443 pinning: checked explicitly (see coverage point 5 above and the direct grep) -- no test asserts a whole-file byte-for-byte reformat on a FIXED file (every fixed-file check goes through Jason.decode!/1 and only asserts the status field's value, never raw bytes), and no test exercises an unrecognized/misspelled flag at all (grepped for --bogus/--Dir/--auto-fix/--diir/unrecognized/unknown flag -- zero hits). Neither ISS-0442's nor ISS-0443's undesired-and-flagged-for-fix behaviour is pinned as an expectation anywhere in this suite. No MINOR finding needed here.

OVERALL: PASS. All 9 coverage points have a genuinely discriminating test verified by reading the code directly. Two independently-reproduced mutants (M1, M2) exactly match TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts and failing-test sets, both applied and measured in a throwaway worktree that was fully removed and left no residue, both reverts verified via git status --porcelain and a green re-run, and the main working tree's lib/ and test/ were never mutated at any point during this gate. No mutant residue found anywhere in the tree (lib/ byte-identical to the REVIEWER-passed commit; no stray test/fixtures files). No test pins ISS-0442/ISS-0443's undesired behaviour.
